steps.title: Implement bubble sort
steps.description: Write a function that sorts an array using the bubble sort algorithm. Repeatedly step through the array, comparing adjacent elements and swapping them if they are in the wrong order.
hints: Use nested loops: outer loop for passes, inner loop for comparisons
After each pass, the largest element bubbles to the end
Optimize: stop early if no swaps occur in a pass

verification.failureMessage: Implement bubble sort and display the sorted array.

steps.title: Implement selection sort
steps.description: Write a selection sort function that divides the array into sorted and unsorted regions, repeatedly selecting the smallest element from the unsorted region and adding it to the sorted region.
hints: Find the minimum element in the unsorted portion
Swap it with the first unsorted element
Advance the boundary between sorted and unsorted regions

verification.failureMessage: Implement selection sort and display the sorted array.

steps.title: Implement merge sort
steps.description: Write a merge sort function that recursively divides the array into halves, sorts each half, and merges them back together. This is a classic divide-and-conquer algorithm.
hints: Base case: arrays with 0 or 1 elements are already sorted
Split the array in half and recursively sort each half
The merge function combines two sorted arrays into one

steps.title: Implement quick sort
steps.description: Write a quick sort function that picks a pivot element, partitions the array around it, and recursively sorts the sub-arrays. Quick sort is one of the most efficient sorting algorithms.
hints: Choose a pivot (last element, first element, or median-of-three)
Partition: rearrange so elements < pivot come before it, > pivot after
Recursively sort the sub-arrays on either side of the pivot

verification.failureMessage: Implement quick sort with partitioning and recursion.

steps.title: Compare sorting algorithm performance
steps.description: Create a test that generates a large random array and times each sorting algorithm. Display the time each algorithm takes and verify all produce the same sorted result.
hints: Generate a random array of at least 1000 elements
Copy the array before sorting (sorting modifies in-place)
Use timing functions to measure execution time

verification.successMessage: All sorting algorithms implemented and compared!
verification.failureMessage: Test all algorithms with timing comparison.
